text: That afternoon we went to Saxe Coburg Square, a poor little place where Wilsons shop stood with three gilt balls above the door. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes walked slowly up the street, then came back and thumped the pavement two or three times with his stick. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he knocked at the shop door, and a bright young man opened it and asked him to step in. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes only asked the way to the Strand, but it was the knees of the young mans trousers that he really wanted to see. <break time="0.8s" /> He is, in my opinion, the fourth smartest man in London, Holmes said as we walked away from the shop. <break time="0.8s" /> We turned the corner and found a busy street full of fine shops, offices, and a branch of the City and Suburban Bank. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes studied the buildings carefully and then spent the rest of the afternoon listening to violin music at a concert hall. <break time="0.8s" /> That evening he told me that a serious crime was being planned and that it would take place that very night. <break time="0.8s" /> Come to Baker Street at ten, he said, and please bring your army revolver, because there may be some danger. <break time="0.8s" /> I went home puzzled, for although I had seen and heard everything that he had, I still understood nothing.
